requirement:
When the backend and model support prompt caching, every provider request MUST
place one cache checkpoint after the system prompt of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and another at the end of its last
message, so each request reuses the tool definitions and system prompt that
earlier assessments of its kind sent, and the conversation its own earlier
requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT change the content of a request.
rationale:
I found no gap. The sources carry out each obligation and test it.

**Obligations**
1. When the backend and model support caching, every provider request MUST place a checkpoint after the system prompt.
2. In that case it MUST also place a checkpoint at the end of its last message.
3. Checkpoints MUST NOT change the content of a request.

**Implementation**
- `RigProvider::connect` (src/authoring/providers.rs:110-145) decides whether caching applies. Bedrock sets it through `bedrock_caches(model)`, which is true only for the Claude and Nova families. Ollama is always false.
- `CompletionProvider::complete` (src/authoring/providers.rs:198-220) is the one request path I read. When `self.caches` is set, it calls `place_cache_checkpoints(&mut request)` before every `model.call`, so the placement applies to every request on this path.
- `place_cache_checkpoints` (src/authoring/providers.rs:315-323) sets only `request.options.cache = Some(CacheRetention::Short)`. It leaves message content, preamble and history untouched, which meets obligation 3.
- The vendored rig-bedrock then places the `cachePoint` blocks as separate blocks. Its own test `cache_points_follow_what_the_request_sends` shows one block after the system prompt and one at the end of the last message. It also shows the vendored patch allows checkpoints after reasoning turns.
- All the implementing functions carry `{impl}` references. The vendored crate is third-party code, so I did not treat its missing reference as a gap.

**Tests**
- `cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models` (src/authoring/providers.rs:592-625) covers the supported-model decision. It checks Claude, a Claude inference-profile ARN and Nova as cached, and Llama and an unknown model as not cached. It also checks that only the cache option changes on the request, and that it still applies after a reasoning turn.
- `claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage` (tests/authoring_cli.rs:1777-1820) runs the real CLI against a fake Bedrock server and asserts the following on both request bodies:
  - the system array is the system text followed by one checkpoint;
  - the last message ends with a checkpoint;
  - there are exactly two `cachePoint`s in total.
- That test also covers the second request, which follows a reasoning turn and still ends in a checkpoint.
- The same test runs an uncached model and shows that the cached bodies, once the `cachePoint` blocks are stripped, equal the uncached bodies. This verifies that checkpoints do not change content, and that unsupported models get none.
- The helpers `bedrock_run` and `without_cache_points` carry `{test}` references.

The "reuses earlier requests' content" wording states the purpose of the checkpoints. It adds no separate testable obligation.
